answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, switching primary vendor (memory_c2's cost win notwithstanding) or deferring past a non-auto-renewing expiry both raise delivery risk unacceptably. Adding a second source is valuable but exceeds this cycle's single-decision capacity and doesn't address the 18% cost mandate. Negotiating terms with the incumbent — renegotiation backed by market benchmarking plus a multi-year commitment (memory_c4, memory_c6) — targets the mandated cost cut while preserving the stable integration record (memory_c1). I verify c4 and c6 because they carry the load of this choice; c1/c2 are supporting context only. Confidence is moderate until the archived records confirm the magnitude and conditions of those savings.
